subject: mattpocock_skills:skill:skills/engineering/code-review#no-cross-axis-rerank
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-20 (conversation), deferred review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3, accepting the report's reject recommendation. Ours keeps the spec and quality verdicts distinct when those roles are dispatched separately and asks for every finding with its severity, then leaves the coordinator to filter and dispose of the findings across the review; its combined mode covers both axes under one verdict. A standing ban on ordering findings across axes would take that judgement from the coordinator, which owns disposition of findings, and the owner declined it (.claude/skills/review/SKILL.md:13-14; .claude/skills/review/references/review-contract.md:9-11; .claude/skills/review/references/code.md:4-5; AGENTS.md:51-52).

subject: mattpocock_skills:skill:skills/engineering/code-review#three-dot-merge-base
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-20 (conversation), deferred review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3. Adopted as the narrower variant merge-base-default-scope: with no base named or recorded, code review now defaults to the branch's merge-base with its base branch, through the working tree, committed and uncommitted. The sentence is in code review's scope paragraph (.claude/skills/review/references/code.md:11-14), which the review skill loads for every code mode (.claude/skills/review/SKILL.md:29-30), dispatched reviewers follow (.claude/skills/review/references/review-contract.md:5-7) and the implement playbook's full review path uses (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/implement/task-engine.md:69-72). A recorded base is, for example, the implement playbook's SCOPE_BASE, recorded once in its ledger and passed to every review package (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/implement/task-engine.md:14; .claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/implement/task-engine.md:22-27). Upstream always diffs three-dot from the fixed point the user gives, committed work only, and asks for one when none is given; ours keeps a named or recorded base as given and uses the merge-base only as the default, so unrelated base-branch changes stay out without a question (U-02, U-06).
modification: Adopted as merge-base-default-scope: the merge-base is the default when no base is named, obviously supplied or recorded, and the diff runs through the working tree. Upstream diffs every fixed point three-dot against its merge-base, committed work only, and asks for a fixed point when none is given.

subject: mattpocock_skills:skill:skills/engineering/code-review#parallel-subagents
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-20 (conversation), deferred review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3, accepting the report's reject recommendation. Ours chooses per review between an inline or combined review and separately dispatched spec and quality roles, invokes substantive review on the light path only when needed, and lets independent reviews run concurrently on a stable snapshot when permitted; AGENTS.md matches review to consequences and leaves when to delegate to mvp-mode, keeping small work local. Always running the two axes as parallel subagents is an absolute rule for a choice that depends on the work (C-14, U-07, S-08) (.claude/skills/review/references/code.md:4-7; .claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/implement/task-engine.md:65-72; AGENTS.md:39-40; AGENTS.md:47-48).

subject: mattpocock_skills:skill:skills/engineering/code-review#capped-reviewer-report
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-20 (conversation), deferred review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3, accepting the report's reject recommendation. Ours asks a critic for a thorough opinion and every finding with its severity, filtered afterwards, and gives each role a fixed output shape rather than a length; a fixed word cap can suppress findings (C-11) and is an invented numerical threshold, which the writing principles prune (.claude/skills/review/SKILL.md:12-14; .claude/skills/review/references/review-contract.md:25-31; .claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:35-36).

subject: mattpocock_skills:skill:skills/engineering/code-review#per-axis-summary-line
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-20 (conversation), deferred review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3, accepting the report's reject recommendation. Ours ends each dispatched role with its own verdict and issues, and a code review with its findings, actual checks, limits and a justified verdict, saying plainly when none were found. A closing line of per-axis counts and the worst issue in each adds a synthesis, but as a mandatory part of every review it is an extra fixed format the owner declined; the writing principles keep only what changes decisions (.claude/skills/review/references/review-contract.md:13-31; .claude/skills/review/references/code.md:56-57; .claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:32-36).

subject: mattpocock_skills:skill:skills/engineering/code-review#code-smell-catalog
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-20 (conversation), deferred review, bead cr-r2pa.3.3, accepting the report's reject recommendation. Ours reviews against the coding standards the repository documents, says so when it documents none, and reports actionable defects with a trigger and consequence; preference alone is not a finding. It carries no general smell catalogue applied to every change. Some specific signs live instead in the principle whose situation they belong to, such as fix-root-causes' workaround that needs a long justifying comment (routed for diagnosing or fixing a failure), and a dispatched reviewer is given the principles the change falls under; that keeps each sign where it acts rather than in a fixed list in the review (.claude/skills/review/references/code.md:41-45; .claude/skills/review/references/code.md:51-54; .claude/skills/review/SKILL.md:23; .claude/skills/delegation/SKILL.md:46-48; .claude/skills/mvp-mode/principles/fix-root-causes.md:15-16; .claude/skills/mvp-mode/SKILL.md:85).
